videos.title: Preferred stock
videos.take: Preferred shares get dividend and liquidation preferences; mandatorily redeemable preferred is a liability

scenes.say: To fund a second plant without more debt, Bluestem sells preferred stock to a regional investment fund.

sub: and in liquidation, usually no vote
scenes.say: Preferred stock gives its holders priority over common shareholders for dividends and in liquidation, in exchange for giving up voting rights and, usually, upside.

scenes.heading: Common features
items: Redeemable on a date or at holder's option
scenes.say: Features vary. Cumulative preferred carries missed dividends forward. Participating preferred shares in extra dividends with common. Convertible preferred can become common shares. Callable preferred can be bought back by the company; redeemable preferred must be.

scenes.heading: Bluestem's preferred issue
scenes.say: Bluestem issues 5,000 shares of $100 par, six percent cumulative preferred stock at par, raising $500,000. The annual preferred dividend is $30,000.

sub: Required to be repaid on a set date:
scenes.say: Watch out: preferred stock that must be redeemed on a fixed date is a liability, not equity, and its dividends are interest expense. Substance over legal form.

scenes.q: Preferred stock that must be redeemed for cash in 2033 is reported as:
scenes.say: Quick check. Preferred stock that must be redeemed for cash in 2033 is reported as what? Pause and pick.

videos.title: Cash dividends
videos.take: A dividend becomes a liability when declared; the record date sets who receives it

scenes.say: Bluestem's board declares its first common dividend: forty cents a share.

scenes.heading: Three dates
scenes.say: Three dates matter. On the declaration date, the board's vote creates a liability. The record date fixes which shareholders receive it; no entry. On the payment date, cash goes out.

scenes.heading: Declaration: 503,000 shares × $0.40
scenes.say: On declaration, Bluestem debits Retained Earnings, or a Dividends account closed to it, and credits Dividends Payable for $201,200.

scenes.heading: Payment
scenes.say: On the payment date, the liability is paid. Dividends are never an expense.
To pay a cash dividend, a company needs enough retained earnings, under most state laws, and enough cash. Profitable companies can still be short of cash.

scenes.q: On which date is a dividend liability recorded?
scenes.say: Quick check. On which date is a dividend liability recorded? Pause and pick.

videos.title: Dividend preferences
videos.take: Cumulative preferred receives arrears and the current dividend before common gets anything

scenes.say: In a bad year, Bluestem skipped the preferred dividend. This year the board declares $120,000. Who gets what?
Missed dividends on cumulative preferred are dividends in arrears. They're not a liability until declared, but they must be disclosed in the notes.

scenes.heading: Allocating $120,000
scenes.say: Cumulative preferred first gets last year's $30,000 of arrears, then this year's $30,000. That's $60,000. The remaining $60,000 goes to common shareholders.
If the preferred were noncumulative, the missed dividend would be lost forever: preferred would get $30,000 and common $90,000.
Participating preferred would also share in dividends above a basic rate for common. It's rare in practice.

scenes.q: 6% cumulative preferred, $200,000 par, 2 years in arrears. Dividends declared $50,000. Amount to common?
scenes.say: Quick check. Six percent cumulative preferred, two hundred thousand par, two years in arrears. Dividends declared fifty thousand. Amount to common? Pause and pick.
scenes.reveal: It's B, $14,000: preferred takes three years at $12,000.

videos.title: Property and liquidating dividends
videos.take: Property dividends are recorded at fair value with a gain or loss; liquidating dividends return paid-in capital

scenes.say: Dividends don't have to be cash.
A property dividend pays shareholders in noncash assets, like shares of another company. It's measured at the fair value of the assets distributed.

scenes.heading: Distributing an investment
scenes.say: Bluestem distributes shares it owns in a supplier, carried at $50,000 but worth $65,000. First it remeasures them to fair value, recognizing a $15,000 gain. Then it declares a $65,000 property dividend.
A liquidating dividend returns contributed capital, not earnings. It's debited to paid-in capital, and shareholders must be told the source. Mining companies winding down a mine often pay them.
Any dividend not based on retained earnings is a return of capital and must be identified as such.

scenes.q: Land carried at $80,000, fair value $70,000, is distributed as a dividend. Result?
scenes.say: Quick check. Land carried at eighty thousand, fair value seventy thousand, is distributed as a dividend. Result? Pause and pick.
scenes.reveal: It's B: a $10,000 loss and a $70,000 dividend.

videos.title: Stock dividends and stock splits
videos.take: Small stock dividends move fair value from retained earnings to paid-in capital; splits need no entry

scenes.say: Bluestem wants to reward shareholders without spending cash. It declares a ten percent stock dividend.

scenes.heading: Small stock dividend: 10%
rows: To paid-in capital in excess of par
scenes.say: Ten percent of 503,000 shares is 50,300 new shares. For a small stock dividend, under twenty to twenty-five percent, the shares' fair value of $15 each, $754,500, moves from retained earnings: $50,300 to common stock at par and $704,200 to paid-in capital.
A large stock dividend, over twenty to twenty-five percent, transfers only par value from retained earnings, because it behaves more like a split and the share price will drop.

scenes.heading: Stock dividend vs stock split
scenes.say: A stock split, like two for one, doubles the shares and halves the par value. No account balances change, so there's no entry. Neither a stock dividend nor a split changes total equity or anyone's ownership percentage.
Both lower the price per share, which can broaden ownership. A stock dividend also formally capitalizes retained earnings.

scenes.q: A 2-for-1 stock split affects total stockholders' equity by:
scenes.say: Quick check. A two-for-one stock split affects total stockholders' equity how? Pause and pick.

videos.title: Restrictions and payout
videos.take: Disclose retained earnings restrictions; payout ratio shows how much of income is paid out

scenes.say: Bluestem's bond indenture limits how much it can pay in dividends.

Retained earnings can be restricted by law, for example to the cost of treasury stock held, or by contract, like Bluestem's bond covenant. Restrictions are usually disclosed in the notes rather than recorded.
Bluestem's bonds limit dividends to forty percent of net income while they're outstanding. The note discloses the restriction and how much is still available.

scenes.heading: Payout ratio, 2029
scenes.say: The payout ratio is cash dividends to common over net income available to common: $201,200 over $960,000, twenty-one percent, well within the covenant.
Growing companies like Bluestem keep most of their earnings to reinvest. Mature companies tend to pay out more.

scenes.q: Net income $500,000; preferred dividends $50,000; common dividends $135,000. Payout ratio?
scenes.say: Quick check. Net income five hundred thousand; preferred dividends fifty thousand; common dividends one thirty-five thousand. Payout ratio? Pause and pick.
scenes.reveal: It's B, thirty percent: one thirty-five over four fifty.
